Three things the next attempt will hit.

(1) Upstream's `@[category test, AMS 11]` attribute is DROPPED here, as it already was on parts.i. It is defined in `FormalConjecturesUtil`, which is not vendored and is not a Mathlib declaration, so keeping it would be a hard elaboration error. This is the one deviation from verbatim and it is deliberate; the file header now says so explicitly. If the project ever wants those attributes, it needs FormalConjecturesUtil vendored or a local stub of the `category`/`AMS` attribute syntax, and that is a new dependency decision, not something an attempt should take on its own.

(2) `isGoodFor_1_low_values` is categorically different from the other three declarations in upstream 359.lean. It is `@[category test]`, not `@[category research open]`: it is a FINITE, DECIDABLE, actually-provable fact (the first 8 terms of the sequence), not an open conjecture. Its `sorry` is a to-do, not an advertised open statement. The file header's blanket "do not fix the sorry" language is correct for parts.i and would be wrong if applied to this one; the header now distinguishes them. So this theorem is a genuine proof target, unlike everything else vendored from 359 so far.

(3) The statement is set-image equality (`A '' Set.Iic 7 = {1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 15}` as `Set ℕ`), NOT a list or a per-index conjunction, so it is not `decide`-able as written. A proof has to first pin `A 0 .. A 7` pointwise out of `hA` (each step is an `IsLeast` obligation over the `∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a b, A i` sum set), then convert eight pointwise values into the image equality via `Set.image` unfolding on `Set.Iic 7 = {0,1,...,7}`. The per-index extraction is the expensive half: each `IsLeast` gives a lower bound plus a minimality side that must rule out every smaller candidate as a consecutive-sum.

work.what:
Prove (discharge the `sorry` in) the theorem `erdos_359.variants.isGoodFor_1_low_values` in lean/Erdos/359.lean of the Zeta repo. Unlike the other Erdős 359 statements in that file, this one is NOT an open conjecture: upstream formal-conjectures marks it `@[category test]`, it is a finite decidable fact, and its `sorry` is a to-do that should be closed.

The file already contains, vendored verbatim from formal-conjectures/359.lean, the definition it depends on:

  def IsGoodFor (A : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Prop := A 0 = n ∧ StrictMono A ∧
    ∀ j, IsLeast
      {m : ℕ | A j < m ∧ ∀ a b, Finset.Icc a b ⊆ Finset.Iic j → m ≠ ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a b, A i}
      (A <| j + 1)

and the theorem to prove, whose statement must NOT be restated, generalised, weakened or specialised:

  /-- Suppose monotone sequence $A$ satisfies the following: `A 0 = 1` and for all `j`, `A (j + 1)` is the
  smallest natural number that cannot be written as a sum of consecutive terms of `A 0, ..., A j`.
  Then the first few terms of $A$ are $1,2,4,5,8,10,14,15,...$. -/
  theorem erdos_359.variants.isGoodFor_1_low_values (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : IsGoodFor A 1) :
      A '' (Set.Iic 7) = {1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 15} := by
    sorry

The file opens with `import Mathlib` and `open Filter`. Shape of the proof: destructure `hA` into `A 0 = 1`, `StrictMono A`, and the per-`j` `IsLeast`; use the `IsLeast` at j = 0..6 to pin `A 1 = 2, A 2 = 4, A 3 = 5, A 4 = 8, A 5 = 10, A 6 = 14, A 7 = 15` one index at a time (the membership half gives that the value is not a consecutive sum and exceeds `A j`; the lower-bound half rules out each smaller candidate, which is a finite check over `Finset.Icc a b ⊆ Finset.Iic j`); then turn the eight pointwise values into the set-image equality by rewriting `Set.Iic 7` as the explicit finite set `{0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7}` and pushing `Set.image` through it. Note the goal is `Set ℕ` equality, so plain `decide` does not apply directly; the decidable content is in the per-index candidate elimination.

Build one file rather than running a full `lake build` (which may try to rebuild Mathlib into the shared read-only packages directory): from the `lean/` directory run
  LP=$(ls -d .lake/packages/*/.lake/build/lib/lean | tr '\n' ':') && env LEAN_PATH="$LP" lean Erdos/359.lean
Success means the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning for `isGoodFor_1_low_values` is gone while the one for `erdos_359.parts.i` (a genuinely open statement) remains, and there are no errors.

edges.why: The theorem has to exist in lean/Erdos/359.lean with its `sorry` before anything can discharge that `sorry`.
